PullRequest.Title: agentHost: add fork_session server tool
PullRequest.Body:
Adds a `fork_session` Agent Host server tool so an agent can fork a chat the way the user's Fork action does.

## What

An agent can call `fork_session` to fork its own chat, or any linked chat, at the last completed turn. The fork is a new nested chat with the copied history, optionally started with a `prompt`. The tool is deferred, asks for confirmation, and is offered only to agents that advertise `multipleChats.fork` (Copilot, Claude, Codex).

## Changes

- `serverToolNames.ts`, `sessionServerTools.ts`: new `fork_session` tool (optional `session`, `prompt`, `title`). It goes through `createChat` with `fork: { source, turnId }`, the same path as the UI Fork and AHP `createChat`, so origin, folders and config match. The model follows the UI (`activeTurn ?? lastTurn`). With a `prompt` it starts the fork with the same delegation metadata as `create_session`.
- It is in `sessionConfirmationToolNames`, counts against the per-session chat-creation limit (agent orchestration limits), and is refused at call time if the agent cannot fork.
- `agentService.ts`, `agentServiceFoundation.ts`: `createChat` passes `fork` through; `supportsChatForks` is wired to `capabilities.multipleChats.fork`.
- `AGENTS.md`: documents the tool.
- 19 prompt baselines gain the additive `fork_session` entry (about 21 lines each, 23 in 10 files): the standard tool envelope, the name, one short description that disambiguates it from `create_session`, and the three parameter descriptions. The eager tool set is unchanged.

## Notes for reviewers

- Forking a linked chat of another session creates the fork in that session with the caller's credentials, like `create_session` and `send_message`. This is intended.
- No new setting or policy: the tool is covered by session-tool confirmation, the orchestration limits and the fork capability gate. No new UI.
- Known pre-existing limitation, not changed here: agent host tools, including this one, are not gated by `chat.disableAIFeatures`. That is tracked separately.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/**/*.test.js"`: 15845 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "serverToolGroups deferral budget|toolSearchDeferral"`: passing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: clean.
- New recorded E2E `server tool: fork_session forks the calling chat with its history and runs the prompt`: replays on Copilot, Claude and Codex.
- Live in Code OSS (agent calls `fork_session`; the fork appears as a nested session with the copied history and runs the prompt): passes; VoiceOver not run; Claude and Codex covered by the E2E replay only.
- Cross-platform Azure run (definition 727): pending.

Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of @sandy081

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new explicit-session branch unconditionally awaits listSessions before reading the selected chat. Its accessor resolves to AgentService.listSessions, whose settled computations are discarded; the catalog reader batches 400 sessions with concurrency four. The existing getSession accessor supplies one session's recorded chats, and live targets can use its summary fast path. Exact elapsed time depends on catalog size and fallback eligibility.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Session-catalog database batch reads, decoded metadata objects for unrelated sessions, and provider/session-storage reads for ineligible rows.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N visible registered sessions, each non-overlapping explicit fork requests ceil(N/400) catalog batches and reconstructs O(N) metadata; F ineligible rows add F fallback resolutions limited to four concurrently. Concurrent calls in the same catalog mode coalesce, but successive forks recompute the catalog.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased fork and parent-agent continuation latency, unnecessary database/provider I/O, and catalog-sized allocation work.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The existing UI fork used the known source chat and invoked createChat without enumerating unrelated sessions. No fork_session handler existed. The new tool's omitted-session branch also resolves ownership directly without a listing.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new agent-triggered fork path performs a complete session-catalog computation before every non-overlapping invocation with an explicit session link, even when that source is already loaded. Only concurrent listings share a computation; a warm source does not avoid the global read.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1721 awaits listSessions whenever session is supplied, including a link to the already-running calling session. Lines 1722 and 1727 then consume only the selected session and its chats. The pre-existing UI fork path in baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.forkChat calls connection.createChat directly without a whole-catalog listing.
Findings.Title: Resolve explicit fork targets without listing the whole catalog
Findings.Impact: Forking a linked chat in a host with a large saved-session catalog delays the tool result and the calling agent's continuation on unrelated catalog I/O and metadata reconstruction, even if the source chat is warm. Ineligible catalog rows can also cause unrelated provider and session-database reads.
Findings.Evidence: AgentService's sessionServerToolAccessor.listSessions calls this.listSessions (agentService.ts:2357). listSessions and _startSessionListComputation (5527-5570, 5648-5674) share in-flight work but clear settled entries. _computeSessions reads all visible registered sessions and calls _catalogListReader.readMany (5706-5733); agentHostCatalogListReader.ts:94-103 issues ceil(N/400) readSessionListCatalogs batches with Limiter(4), then decodes metadata for all N sessions. Ineligible rows additionally use provider/session-storage fallbacks under Limiter(4) (agentService.ts:5779-5835). In contrast, accessor.getSession resolves to _getSessionMetadata (3541-3561), which looks up one registry entry and, for a live source, returns its summary including recorded chats (3592-3611). resolveLinkedChat and resolveDefaultChat accept that single metadata entry.
Findings.Recommendation: Parse the explicit link with the existing parser and resolve its session through the existing getSession accessor, retaining equivalent known/visible-session validation and resolving the chat against that session's recorded chats. At minimum, fast-path explicit links to the already-known calling session so they do not enumerate unrelated sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Advertise and discover fork_session during session materialization and ordinary agent turns
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host constructs and publishes the tool catalog before provider tool availability; it does not read fork history or create a chat merely to advertise this definition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish one additional capability-gated tool definition and pass its schema through the existing provider tool protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional fixed-size definition per eligible materialized session; full schema is deferred when tool search is active, and included through the existing eager fallback when tool search is off.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalog publication and provider serialization existed, without this one tool definition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded additional catalog serialization; no history, filesystem, subprocess, or model-discovery operation is started by the new capability check.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of eligible sessions and provider requests; definition size is fixed, not proportional to conversation history or saved-session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous catalog construction and publication; no new concurrent tasks or subprocesses.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tool membership is materialized; advertisement compares the catalog before dispatching. Capability checks read provider descriptors. Existing tool-search deferral remains active; no eager discovery cache is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced definition registration, capability gate, host advertisement deduplication, and provider deferral.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No token or timing measurements; the added payload is bounded. Prompt snapshots are fixtures, not additional production requests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: fixed-size additive metadata and unchanged loading policy do not establish expensive eager execution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fork the calling chat without an explicit session link or an initial prompt
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Confirmation and the creation-limit check precede ownership resolution. Source context must resolve, then the existing createChat fork, provider backing creation, and persistence must complete before returning the fork link.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source events when the reconstruction memo misses, resolve the fork boundary, call sessions.fork, and copy the session database with VACUUM INTO.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fork RPC and at most one database copy per created fork; source event reads page at 1000 events and are memoized by primary/all scope until invalidation. No host-wide session listing for omitted session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These exact boundary operations already ran for UI/AHP forks. The diff adds an explicit agent tool entry point, not a per-turn or per-event multiplier.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Source inspection, SDK fork, and database copy are awaited before chat publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the source transcript, fork it through the SDK, and persist inherited settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transcript read and one SDK fork per fork attempt; history work scales with source transcript bytes. No live Query is created merely to bind an inherited fork.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existing provider fork flow served UI/AHP createChat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transcript inspection, fork creation, and setting persistence precede return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read source thread history, call thread/fork, read retained fork history to map turn IDs, and optionally copy a managed working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source history read and, when turn mapping is nonempty, one fork history read. Each paginated history read performs one thread/read plus its sequential thread/turns/list pages; legacy history uses a second thread/read. One thread/fork and an optional recursive directory copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: UI/AHP forks used the same source/fork history reads, thread creation, and optional managed-directory copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing fork preparation and mapping operations are awaited; app-server creation may involve its filesystem helper.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the new chat backing, title, launch directories, catalog, and inherited configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One creation pipeline per fork, with existing metadata writes and catalog serialization; source turn objects are shallowly copied once up to the boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing createChat forks performed the same persistence and turn-ID remapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Durable backing and metadata precede chat publication and the tool result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Source history turns/events/bytes, optional managed-directory bytes, and number of requested forks. Successful creations share the existing default limit of 50 chats per calling session per hour.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host catalog mutation serializes creation per target session. Copilot fork setup uses a session sequencer separate from active per-chat turn queues; Claude reads the source without waiting for its active-turn sequencer; Codex serializes thread creation by overlapping workspace roots on Linux. There is no newly introduced collection-wide burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: For a running caller, getChatContext returns existing state references rather than cloning/reloading history. resolveChatState shares in-flight resolution and retains successful state; failed resolutions can retry. Copilot event reconstruction is separately memoized. Scratch allocation is skipped for fork options.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the new handler through ownership, warm-state resolution, creation reservations, provider forks, persistence, and rollback ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History size and SDK fork/copy duration are unmeasured; provider internals are reviewed through their repository wrappers, not executed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: history copying and backing creation are required by the requested fork and preserve the existing UI/AHP mechanism. The context lookup does not introduce a second warm-source history read.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fork an explicitly linked session or nested chat, including an already-warm source
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new handler first waits for the entire session listing to validate one target, then resolves source context and runs the existing fork pipeline. The parent agent cannot continue past the tool until those steps finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate visible registered sessions, read and decode their catalog metadata, and select one source session/chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One whole-catalog computation per non-overlapping explicit fork. For N visible registered sessions, ceil(N/400) successful catalog batches run with concurrency four; metadata reconstruction covers all N. Concurrent listings in the same mode share their computation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing UI fork directly used its known source and called createChat without a catalog listing. The new omitted-session branch likewise avoids the listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All listing work must finish before even the selected source context is read or the fork starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve ineligible catalog entries through provider/session-state fallbacks; on bulk-read failure, fall back to target-specific catalog reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F ineligible entries require F fallback resolutions with a four-task limiter. A successful catalog listing is batched, not one provider call per saved session. Bulk database failure can additionally trigger N per-session catalog fallback reads, also limited to four.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fallback mechanisms already existed for list_sessions, but UI forking did not put a whole listing and its unrelated fallback rows on the fork path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unrelated fallback rows delay target validation and hence the fork result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore a cold source session and resolve the addressed peer's backing/history when necessary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared restore per source session and one shared resolution per addressed chat. A cold peer's owning-session restore reads the default chat first, then resolves the selected peer; warm targets avoid these history restores. Provider-specific fork operations remain as described in the calling-chat scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These restoration APIs and per-key coalescing were already used for session opening/context inspection; existing UI fork normally addressed an already-open source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Target restoration and source history are required before choosing the completed boundary and creating the fork.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N visible saved sessions, F ineligible catalog rows, source history size, and repeated explicit fork invocations. Catalog cost is independent of the selected source's warmth.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog batches and provider fallbacks are each limited to four. Same-mode concurrent listings coalesce, while sequential explicit forks recompute. Existing per-session fork catalog serialization applies only after target lookup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: listSessions retains only in-flight/trailing computations, not settled successful results. Warm source state therefore does not avoid the newly added global catalog read. Cold target restores and chat resolution coalesce per key; failures are retriable, not permanent negative-cache entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the unconditional changed await, exact accessor binding, catalog batch size, limiters, settled-entry cleanup, and target-scoped getSession alternative were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured latency; the largest catalogs and fallback prevalence vary. That affects magnitude, not the established catalog-sized I/O and critical-path dependency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity eager-work regression at sessionServerTools.ts:1721: one explicit target lookup now unnecessarily waits on the entire catalog. Target-scoped resolution is already available.

Scenarios.Scenario: Fork with an optional prompt, preserving the source custom agent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fork creation completes first. startPrompt then synchronously admits a turn through the existing turn service; provider send and model completion are asynchronous and are not awaited by the tool result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the fork's working directories, capture one turn-start checkpoint, apply agent/model selection, and prepare the selected provider runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One newly requested turn pipeline per supplied prompt; existing checkpoint work scales with its working directories. Providers reuse shared clients/connections; Claude's inherited backing materializes its live Query on this first send rather than on fork binding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing create_session prompts and UI fork initial messages used the same turn admission, checkpoint, selection, and send pipeline. A fork without a prompt performs no turn-start work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This work affects the fork's first response, but is off the parent tool-result path after turn admission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the explicitly supplied prompt to the fork's provider; first use can materialize/resume its provider runtime using the existing SDK-loading policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One requested child turn, with its normal model/tool requests. No polling or duplicate prompt send is introduced. Shared provider clients, installed SDKs, and connections remain reusable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: UI fork-with-message and create_session already started provider turns through this infrastructure; this tool adds the explicitly requested fork prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model response latency belongs to the child turn; the parent and child can continue concurrently after the fork tool returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of explicit prompts, selected provider startup state, history/context bytes, and working directories. One invocation creates one fork and at most one child turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parent and child turns can overlap, as reflected in the E2E captures. Existing per-chat send queues and Codex workspace-root creation sequencing apply; startPrompt does not await child completion. Creation-rate limiting shares the existing chat limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider client/SDK reuse and chat-specific runtime lifecycle are unchanged. The added AgentSelection is passed into normal turn selection, not an independent discovery cache or retained history copy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: startPrompt delegates to _startSessionMessage, which calls the void startTurnMessage; the side-effects adapter launches _sendTurnMessage without awaiting it. The added custom-agent argument follows this same route.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider startup, checkpoint, and network durations were not measured; no claim of extra request fan-out beyond the explicitly requested child turn.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional regression: one requested prompt starts one existing asynchronous turn pipeline. The added await does not block the parent on model completion, and richer agent metadata alone does not establish repeated expensive work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against base 43d7ea26b3e2c86ceb9422a248bca98b7558d435. Inspected all 32 changed files and all diff pages, including 19 snapshots and three provider captures. Submitted one medium-severity, high-confidence finding for whole-catalog work on explicit fork lookup; rejected speculative history-copy, startup, queue, and retention candidates after tracing caches, grouping, lifecycle, and critical paths. No concrete performance regression fix was identified. Static read-only review; no measured timing claims. The requested performance guide load was output-truncated; learned-regression guidance and repository evidence were available.
